hints: Take natural logarithms of both sides of $8^{3 - 6x} = 4 \times 5^{-2x}$.
Use logarithm laws $\ln(AB) = \ln A + \ln B$ and $\ln(A^B) = B\ln A$ to form a linear equation in $x$.
walkthrough:
Take the natural logarithm of both sides of the equation:
$$\ln\left(8^{3 - 6x}\right) = \ln\left(4 \times 5^{-2x}\right)$$

Apply the product law $\ln(uv) = \ln u + \ln v$ and power law $\ln(u^v) = v\ln u$:
$$(3 - 6x)\ln 8 = \ln 4 + \ln\left(5^{-2x}\right)$$
$$(3 - 6x)\ln 8 = \ln 4 - 2x\ln 5$$

Collect all terms in $x$ on the left-hand side and constants on the right-hand side:
$$2x\ln 5 - 6x\ln 8 = \ln 4 - 3\ln 8$$
$$x(2\ln 5 - 6\ln 8) = \ln 4 - 3\ln 8$$
Multiply both sides by $-1$:
$$x(6\ln 8 - 2\ln 5) = 3\ln 8 - \ln 4$$
